# Natural experiment: what sets AC versus ToW prices

*Step 4 of the AC pricing study (`analysis/AC_STUDY_PLAN.md`). Generated by `analysis/experiments/ac_natural_experiment.py`; every number below comes from that run. Outputs in `analysis/output/ac/`.*

## Headline

Every ToW unit is a copy of an AC unit with identical stats, size, flags, stars and cap, so the pair price ratio isolates how the two modes price the same unit (6593 regular, 5183 commander and 221 staff pairs with prices above 1). The residual after the corps-number ratio, r = log(P_ToW/P_AC) - log(N_AC/N_ToW), has median -0.092 (x0.912) and sd 0.130.

**What makes ToW copies cheaper than their AC originals:**

1. **The corps number sets the spread, not the cut.** The median ToW/AC price ratio is 0.896 (66.2% of copies are cheaper). The ratio N_AC/N_ToW explains 77.6% of the variance of log(P_ToW/P_AC), since prices scale with 1/N in both modes (AC slightly flatter: slope 0.947, 95% CI 0.919-0.981). But the median N ratio is 1.000, so it does not make copies cheaper on average: after it ToW is still x0.912 (median).
2. **That remaining cut is AC's own hand-set corps x class multipliers, which ToW largely undoes.** Measured against a stats-only price curve, the ToW copies sit on the curve (mean premium e_T -0.001) while the AC originals sit 10% above it on average (e_A +0.096) and scatter by corps and class. The ToW price moves 0.75 log points down per log point of the AC corps' premium (corps level, R2 0.61; 0.81 and R2 0.71 with the committed adopted ToW model; 0.69 at corps x class level). So the ~9% average cut is the average AC premium over the common curve, and the corps x class spread of r is mostly the spread of that premium.
3. **Formation rebates play no part.** Neither the unit's own brigade or division rebate nor the corps' full-formation rebate tracks r (|corr| <= 0.09). The mean division rebate (10.9%) matches the average AC premium in size, which fits a design intent ('AC list prices carry roughly what a full division gives back'), but no unit or corps is priced by its actual rebate.
4. **There is no exact generating rule** for regular units: no rounding, no quantised factors, and even one factor per AC corps x class cell leaves a within-cell scatter of sd 5.2% that no stat, size, price level or formation explains. Some corps are clean (within-cell sd 1.7% at the 10th percentile), others noisy (7.3% at the 90th).
5. **Staff generals are near-exact:** price x N is a fixed value per star level in each mode, the ToW value is x0.949 the AC value, and V_ToW(stars)/N_ToW reproduces 66.5% of ToW staff prices exactly. **Commanders** keep their AC mark-up over their regular unit, shrunk but not N-scaled: P_ToW,com = P_ToW,reg + k x (P_AC,com - P_AC,reg), k = 0.83 imperial / 0.88 coalition (median error 2.0%).

**Compact rule** (regular units, usable for corps with no ToW copy; leave-corps-out median error 4.8%, P90 14.5%, exact 1.3%):

```
P_ToW = P_AC x (N_AC/N_ToW)^0.977 x k[side, class] x exp(-0.122 e_A -0.459 e_A,cell)
```

where e_A is the unit's AC premium over the stats curve and e_A,cell its AC corps x class mean (details below).

## Hypotheses (regular units unless stated)

R2 is on r. *R2 in* = plain group means or OLS; *CV* = 10-fold over units; *LCO* = leave-corps-out (10 folds grouped by source AC corps), the test that matters for corps with no ToW copy; n/a where the grouping is the AC corps itself. Groupings are one-hot ridge (alpha 1, i.e. group means shrunk toward their parent). Verdict words grade the LCO R2 (else CV): Major >= 0.5, Substantial >= 0.25, Moderate >= 0.10, Small >= 0.03. Full table: `natural_experiment_effects.csv`.

### Notes per hypothesis

**H1 rebates** (`tools/army_builder_rules.py`: `build_roster_totals`, `group_discount`, `support_divisions`). If ToW = AC minus the formation rebate, r would move one-for-one with log(1 - rebate). Correlations: own brigade +0.065, own division +0.089, corps full-division share +0.006 (corps means +0.102), corps full-brigade share -0.033; the free slopes have the wrong sign or are near 0. With the slope fixed at 1 the R2 is -0.539 (division) and -0.224 (corps), worse than a constant. The corps full-division rebate ranges 5.3%-15.0% (10th-90th percentile) and is unrelated to r. **Rejected.**

**H2 unit attributes.** Class explains 0.12 and side x class 0.25; coalition copies are cut less than imperial ones. Training, speed, size, cap and price level add at most a few percent each; all together reach LCO R2 0.233. The source corps x class cell is the main structure (0.84 in sample, 0.64 CV). Inside those cells (residual sd 5.2%) price level has slope +0.035 (R2 0.052) and size +0.076 (R2 0.072); training, speed, cap, division and brigade add nothing out of sample (CV R2 0.636 for corps x class against 0.643 / 0.623 / 0.643 / 0.632 / 0.624 with them).

**H3 the ToW corps.** ToW corps x class explains 0.58 (CV 0.49) against 0.84 for the source corps x class; adding the source corps as a level gives 0.64 (CV 0.54). Each AC corps feeds exactly one ToW corps, so the source cell nests the ToW cell. r is **not** one factor per ToW corps x class applied to all its source corps: source corps in the same ToW cell get different factors, and those follow each source corps' AC premium (ToW corps x class + cell premium: LCO R2 0.563).

**H4 rounding.** Prices are plain integers: 19.7% (AC) and 19.7% (ToW) are multiples of 5 against 20% by chance, 9.9% / 10.1% multiples of 10; last digits are uniform (chi2 6.1 / 8.8, 9 df). The factors of the 343 tight cells (sd <= 2%) sit no closer to a 0.05 grid than random (0.259 of a step; 0.25 = uniform). One factor k with P_ToW = round(P_AC x k) fits every unit in only 49 of 1171 cells with 2+ units (107 of 6103 units, mostly 2-unit cells by chance; floor 120, ceil 104). The cell-median lookup reproduces 14.5% of prices exactly in cells with 2+ units (14.8% with 3+), but that counts each cell's median unit, exact by construction; leave-one-out it is 5.7%. A per-cell affine fit reaches 14.8% in cells with 3+. Staff P x N is the only near-exact pattern (below). **No rounding and no exact per-cell rule for regular units.**

**H5 the N slope.** Within ToW corps x class (N_ToW fixed, N_AC varying across source corps) the slope of log(P_ToW/P_AC) on log(N_AC/N_ToW) is **0.947** (95% cluster bootstrap over AC corps 0.919-0.981; raw 0.966): not exactly 1. AC prices fall a little less than 1/N relative to ToW (the AC-trained fair model has log N coefficient -0.930). The slope cannot be estimated inside one AC corps, because each AC corps feeds exactly one ToW corps. Once the AC premium is in the rule the fitted exponent is 0.977. Commanders: 1.221 (CI 1.175-1.277), because the commander mark-up is not N-scaled. **Exact price x N invariance holds only for staff generals**, within each mode.

**H6 patch history.** Campaign code explains 0.10 (LCO 0.045), campaign x class 0.49 (LCO 0.220); the faction-key x-class 0.08 (LCO -0.005). These largely restate corps x class. `ntw3_land_units` carries superseded balance-edit rows (inert in game; the first row is loaded) for 876 regular AC units, all in campaigns a11, a17, b11, b17 (1812 and 1814); 514 of them have a matching edit on the ToW copy. Edited units sit 2.4% from their cell's median ratio against 1.3% for unedited ones. Where only the AC key was edited, the ToW price matches the live AC row better in 156 cases and a superseded row in 69. So the ToW copies follow the live AC prices, and the later balance passes edited AC and ToW rows together. Patch history adds noise, not the level.

**H7 AC premium over a stats-fair price.** The fair price is a stats-only ridge model of log(P x N/8) trained on ToW regulars (CV rmse 0.130 log; out of fold by source corps for paired units). e_A = log(P_AC x N_AC/8) - fair and e_T = log(P_ToW x N_ToW/8) - fair, so r = e_T - e_A exactly. Mean e_A +0.096, mean e_T -0.001. Weighted regressions of mean r on mean e_A:

| Level | slope | R2 | sd e_A | sd e_T | slope, AC-trained fair | R2 | slope, adopted ToW model | R2 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| unit | -0.503 | 0.322 | 0.147 | 0.130 | -0.392 | 0.162 | -0.515 | 0.365 |
| cell | -0.692 | 0.484 | 0.120 | 0.093 | -0.611 | 0.282 | -0.649 | 0.498 |
| corps | -0.749 | 0.614 | 0.071 | 0.046 | -0.743 | 0.411 | -0.811 | 0.713 |

A slope of -1 would mean ToW removes the AC premium completely, 0 not at all. At corps level the ToW copies sit within sd 0.046 of the curve while the AC originals scatter sd 0.071. Three fair-price definitions agree: the self-contained ToW-trained proxy, one trained on AC prices with log N free (so the result is not circular), and the committed adopted ToW model (`analysis/output/oof_predictions.csv`, `oof_final`, stats only, 6575 pairs). A noisier fair price attenuates the slopes toward 0, so the true pull toward the curve is if anything stronger. Provisional until step 2's AC model replaces the proxy.

## Rules for P_ToW given P_AC

### Regular units

```
Rule C:  P_ToW = P_AC x (N_AC/N_ToW)^0.977 x k[side, class] x exp(-0.122 e_A -0.459 e_A,cell)
  e_A      = log(P_AC x N_AC / 8) - log fair(stats)   the unit's AC premium over the stats curve
  e_A,cell = mean of e_A over the unit's AC corps x class
```

A whole cell priced x(1 + p) above the curve in AC loses about 58% of that premium (in logs) in ToW; a single unit off its cell's level loses 12% of its own deviation. k is the fitted factor at e_A = 0 and N_AC = N_ToW. Rule B is the simplest readable fallback, with no stats model: P_ToW = P_AC x (N_AC/N_ToW)^0.951 x k_B[side, class].

| D2: per-cell affine a x P_AC + b (in sample) | 3322 | 20.9% | 0.8% | 5.8% | 10.5 |  |

Rule C is adopted: it needs only the AC price, the two corps numbers, side, class and a stats-fair price, so it applies to corps with no ToW copy. Out of sample it cuts the median error from 6.1% (A) and 5.4% (B) to 4.8%, and the P90 from 20.4% to 14.5%. The AC price and the stats curve each carry information the other lacks (A alone 6.1%, F alone 6.6%). Campaign x class (C2) helps a little more but only for corps whose campaign has ToW copies. Exact matches stay rare under every rule; the cell lookup D (1 661 factors) is the ceiling for any one-factor-per-cell rule.

The commander mark-up P_com - P_reg (median -83 gold in AC, -69 in ToW; AC 10th-90th percentile -162 to +80) carries over shrunk by k = 0.83 / 0.88 (imperial / coalition) and is **not** rescaled by the N ratio. That additive, unscaled part is why the commander N slope is 1.22. Commander r on its own: class R2 0.09, stars 0.00, ToW corps x class 0.47, source corps x class 0.70, the regular unit's own r 0.57. 6 commander pairs priced 1 gold on one side are left out.

## AC-only corps: ToW-equivalent prices (model-based)

`ac_only_tow_equivalent.csv` gives every unit of the 17 AC corps without a ToW copy (612 regular, 439 commander and 19 staff rows) an **estimated** ToW-equivalent price: what it would cost in a ToW army at its own corps number (`tow_eq_own_n`) and at N = 8 (`tow_eq_n8`). **These are model estimates, not game data.**

- Regular units: rule C, with the corps' own AC premium measured against the ToW-trained stats curve (fitted on all ToW units; these units were never seen). Fixed artillery uses rule B.
- Commanders: the regular estimate plus k x their AC mark-up.
- Staff: V_ToW(stars)/N for star levels with 10+ pairs, else P_AC x N_AC/N x f.
- Low/high: the 10th/90th percentiles of each rule's out-of-sample residuals (regular: rule C leave-corps-out per arm, infantry -10% / +10%, cavalry -10% / +11%, artillery -12% / +12%).

A corps with a large positive premium (its AC prices well above the stats curve) gets the biggest ToW-equivalent cut; a corps priced near or below the curve keeps close to its AC price at its own N.

## What remains unexplained

- **Within-cell scatter**, sd 5.2% (about 16% of r's variance). It is unrelated to stats, size, price level, training, speed, cap or formation, and it is not rounding. It is largest in a few corps (6. Menou / Damiette (13.2%), 6. Chasteler / VIII.K (14.2%), 9. Soult / Sud (18.1%)) and smallest in others (9. Lecourbe / Rhin.D (0.8%), 11. Liechtenstein / RK (0.9%), 9. Bellegarde / I.K (0.9%)). That points to unit-by-unit hand edits in one mode, of which the superseded 1812/1814 rows are the visible part.
- **About 30% of the cross-validated cell structure** (CV R2 0.64 for the corps x class lookup against LCO R2 0.442 for rule C) is not predictable without the pairs. Part of it is the proxy fair price's own error.
- **Why each AC corps x class premium exists.** This study shows that ToW removes most of it; the AC price model (step 2) should say whether it is systematic (by N, side, era) or hand-set.

## Caveats

- The fair price is a self-contained ridge proxy (CV rmse 0.130 log), weaker than the adopted ToW model. Rerun H7 and rule C once step 2's out-of-fold AC predictions exist.
- The N slope is identified only across source corps inside one ToW corps.
- AC-only estimates at N = 3-4 extrapolate below ToW's corps numbers (5-12) and rely on the fixed 1/N of the fair curve; the interval reflects the pairs' spread, not that extrapolation.
- Fixed artillery (4 pairs) is outside the fair model; its premium is set to 0.
- The commander rule's leave-corps-out score equals its in-sample score (2 parameters). The staff rules are in-sample: one factor, or one value per star level.
